description:
Nathan MacKinnon achieved his first-ever 50-goal season, reaching the mark during a hat trick performance late in the 2023-24 campaign. Starting the game with 48 goals under his belt, MacKinnon's first goal originated from the defensive zone. Demonstrating his explosive speed, he burst out of the zone like a bolt of lightning, effortlessly evading two defenders en route to a breakaway opportunity which he capitalized on with a stellar shot. Securing his 50th goal of the season, MacKinnon once again showcased his blazing speed, darting through the neutral zone to unleash a shot from within the faceoff circle past the netminder. To cap the evening off, MacKinnon mesmerized the crowd once more, weaving through the defense with remarkable agility for yet another breakaway goal, prompting a shower of hats from the delighted home fans.

description:
An incredible skater who can change the outcome of any game, defenseman Cale Makar reminds us of why he is so special during a game in the 2021-22 season against Chicago. Midway through the overtime frame, Makar skates the puck behind the net and around the boards before he turns on a dime outwitting the defender and heads to the net. In tight, he dekes forehand-to-backhand and shelves it for the jaw-dropping goal. At the age of just 23, Makar earned both the James Norris Memorial Trophy and Conn Smythe Trophy in 2021-22 which were both firsts in his young career.

description:
Leon Draisaitl, a recipient of the Art Ross Trophy and Hart Trophy, achieved new personal bests in assists and points in the 2022-23 season. Displaying his exceptional passing skills against the Arizona Coyotes, he showcased an elite ability to distribute the puck in the highlight's opening sequence. Executing a spin near the blueline, he dishes a backhand beauty through multiple defenders to Connor McDavid, who finishes the play with a goal. Finally, during overtime against the Florida Panthers, Draisaitl and McDavid capitalize on a 2-on-1 break, engaging in a give-and-go before Draisaitl score the game-winning goal.

description:
The stakes couldn't have been higher as the Philadelphia Flyers and New York Rangers faced off in game No. 82 of the 2009-10 season. The winner would secure the final spot in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. After a tied game in regulation and a scoreless overtime, it all came down to a shootout. With Claude Giroux scoring in the third round, Flyers goalie Brian Boucher was tasked with stopping the Rangers' final attempt to win the game. Boucher held his ground, not falling for the deke, and quickly shut down the five-hole, stopping the puck. The home crowd and team erupted in celebration as Philadelphia clinched their playoff spot. The Flyers then made an incredible run to the Stanley Cup Final, where they eventually fell in six games to the Chicago Blackhawks.

description:
Connor McDavid is no stranger to lighting the lamp. In the 2022-23 season, he soared to new heights, smashing his previous records with an astonishing 64 goals and 153 points. But McDavid didn't rest on his laurels. The following season, he continued to captivate audiences with his unparalleled speed and finesse, delivering jaw-dropping goals that left spectators in awe. Against the Philadelphia Flyers, he showcased his agility, effortlessly maneuvering around Travis Sanheim before unleashing a shot that found the back of the net. Then, during a powerplay matchup against the Kings, McDavid received a pass near the goal line and casually sniped the puck off the goalie's mask and into the net. And in a showdown with the Wild, McDavid demonstrated his exceptional puck control, receiving a pass in the neutral zone, evading a defender with a slick move, outmaneuvering the sprawling Marc-Andre Fleury, and deftly tucking in a backhander for a sensational goal.

description:
During the 2016-17 season opener in Ottawa, Auston Matthews achieved an unprecedented feat, netting four goals in his NHL debut. This historic performance set the modern-era record for most goals in a player's first game. His initial goal resulted from a Zach Hyman wraparound, placing the puck directly on Matthews' stick in front of the net. His second showcased his skill as he stripped Mark Stone of the puck, maneuvered past Mike Hoffman, and then stripped Erik Karlsson along the boards before capitalizing on the sensational goal. Matthews' third goal came via a Morgan Rielly pass, completing his hat trick early in the second period. His fourth goal, solidifying the record, came from a William Nylander pass during a 2-on-1 play. Matthews concluded his exceptional rookie season with 40 goals, earning both the Calder Trophy and acclaim.

description:
In what many consider the save of the 2024 Stanley Cup Playoffs, Sergei Bobrovsky delivered a spectacular stop during Game 2 of the Eastern Conference First Round against the in-state rival Tampa Bay Lightning. With the score tied at two late in the second period, Bobrovsky slid to the far post anticipating a shot after the puck caromed in that direction. However, when the puck was passed out front instead, Bobrovsky, now turned around, made a desperate lunge and managed to get his outstretched arm on the shot attempt. Throughout the playoffs, Bobrovksy posted a 2.32 GAA while also earning 2 shutouts in winning his first ever Stanley Cup.

description:
In an already illustrious career, Sidney Crosby added another remarkable achievement to his name by reaching the 1,500 career points milestone. This accomplishment solidified his place as the 15th player in the history of the game to attain such a feat. Crosby reached this milestone by scoring two goals and an assist against the Detroit Red Wings. The first goal occurred in the closing seconds of the first period, as Crosby’s relentless forecheck applied pressure on Jake Walman, eventually leading to a turnover. Crosby seized the puck right in front of the net and sniped a backhand shot upstairs. After notching an assist in the second period to hit 1,499 points, Crosby reached the milestone with his second goal of the game during a Penguins power play early in the third period. Kris Letang delivered a pass, and Crosby, positioned at the top of the circle, released a perfectly placed wrist shot top shelf.

description:
Connor Bedard, despite missing 14 games due to injury, led all NHL rookies in goals (22) and points (61), earning him the Calder Trophy. Throughout the season, he captivated fans with his impressive skills, justifying his selection as the first overall pick in the 2023 NHL Draft. In one memorable game against the Blues in St. Louis, he executed "The Michigan," scoring a lacrosse-style goal by backhanding the puck into the top shelf. Just four days later in Chicago, he scored his first-ever overtime goal, electrifying the home crowd. Starting deep in the defensive zone, Bedard picked up speed as he skated up the ice with the puck. With both defensemen retreating, he stopped in the high slot and unleashed a wrist shot that beat the goaltender.

description:
Matty Beniers had a standout rookie season with the Seattle Kraken in 2022-23, earning the Calder Trophy. Dominating the rookie scene, he secured an impressive 160 first-place votes out of 196 available. Beniers led all rookies with 57 points, and his 24 goals tied for the top spot in rookie goal scoring. Beyond his stellar stats, he played significant minutes for the playoff-bound Kraken, averaging over 17 minutes of ice time per game. One highlight from his remarkable season was a brilliant play where Beniers showcased his vision and playmaking skills by delivering a perfect pass to Jaden Schwartz for a backdoor tap-in. Additionally, in a home game against the Washington Capitals, Beniers scored his first overtime winner. Seizing an opportunity right after the initial face-off in the extra frame, he found himself on a breakaway and swiftly snapped a shot through the five-hole for the decisive tally.

description:
A member of the Vegas Golden Knights since their inaugural season, Jonathan Marchessault was an incredible performer during the 2023 Stanley Cup Playoffs earning the Conn Smythe Trophy awarded to the most valuable player in the playoffs. He was second overall in points scored (25), tied for first overall in goals (13, including three game-winners) and led all players in plus/minus (+17). This multi-highlight features some of his contributions throughout the playoffs beginning with Game 6 in the Second Round versus the Edmonton Oilers. In Edmonton on the power play leading 3-2 in the game with under two minutes remaining in the second period, Marchessault scores his third goal for the hatty, helping Vegas pad its lead heading into the third period where they clinched the series to advance to the Western Conference Final. Transitioning to the second play within the multi-highlight, Marchessault scores a huge goal against the Dallas Stars in Game 2 of the Western Conference Final. With just over two minutes to play in the third period and down by one goal, Marchessault receives a great pass from Jack Eichel and buries it to even up the game that Vegas would eventually win in overtime. In the final play, Marchessault gets the scoring started for Vegas in Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final with his first of two in the game. On a power play in the first period, he snaps home a beautiful shot past Sergei Bobrovsky to the delight of the home Vegas crowd. In the five-game Stanley Cup Final, Marchessault registered four goals and four assists.

description:
Jonathan Toews won the 2010 Conn Smythe Trophy as the Stanley Cup Playoffs MVP, leading the Chicago Blackhawks to their first championship in 49 years. Toews displayed defensive excellence and timely scoring throughout the playoffs, earning recognition as the most valuable player.

In the Western Conference Quarterfinals against the Nashville Predators, Toews scored the series-clinching goal. On a power play late in the first period, he drove to the net, collected a rebound off a point shot, and fired it into the net just 24 seconds after Nashville had tied the game.

In the Western Conference Semifinals against the Vancouver Canucks, Toews delivered a game-winning performance with his first career playoff hat trick, giving the Blackhawks a commanding 3-1 lead in the series. Positioned in the slot during a power play, Toews received a pass and snapped it top shelf, securing his third goal of the game.

In the Western Conference Final against the San Jose Sharks, Toews' exceptional defensive play led to a go-ahead goal for Chicago, where he earned an assist. In the third period of a tied Game 3, Toews blocked a shot attempt, sending the puck out to the neutral zone, where Dave Bolland collected it and scored on a breakaway.

description:
In leading his team to their first-ever Stanley Cup championship, captain Aleksander Barkov played a pivotal role in their success. Barkov led all players during the Stanley Cup Playoffs with 34 takeaways and tied for the team lead with 22 points. He excelled in critical situations, whether it was winning a key defensive zone face off, shutting down top offensive opponents, or killing penalties.  
During the Eastern Conference Second Round series against Boston, Barkov scored the game-winning goal in Game 4. In the third period, he battled through Boston defenders, maneuvered the puck into the slot, and, surrounded by three Bruins players, shot it past the netminder. Later in the series, in the clinching Game 6, Barkov blocked a one-timer attempt by David Pastrnak late in the game, securing a one-goal victory.  
In the Stanley Cup Final, Barkov's defensive prowess shone again, leading to a crucial assist on Florida's shorthanded goal. Late in the first period, with the Oilers on the power play, Barkov perfectly read the play, poke-checking the puck at the blueline to force a turnover. He then retrieved the puck, skated it up the ice while fending off a defender, and passed it to Gustav Forsling, who set up Sam Reinhart for a redirection goal. Later in that same Game 3, Barkov scored the game-winning goal on a 2-on-1 break with Evan Rodrigues, firing a wrist shot that went short side.

description:
Since Moritz Seider's debut season in 2021-22, no one on the Detroit Red Wings has averaged more ice time per game than him. As a key member of the defensive core, he frequently shoulders the responsibility of shutting down the opposing team's top offensive threats. One standout moment from the 2022-23 season occurred during a game against the Boston Bruins when Seider not only exhibited his defensive abilities but also showcased his offensive skills. While defending against a Bruins power play, Seider managed to strip David Pastrnak of the puck at the Red Wings' blue line, leading to a breakaway opportunity. Breaking down the ice, he shielded the puck from the backpressure and ripped a backhander top shelf for the unassisted shorty.

description:
Larry Robinson kicked off the scoring in Game 5 of the 1978 Stanley Cup Final with a spectacular end-to-end rush. Starting from behind the Canadiens' net, Robinson charged up the ice with speed, weaving around multiple Bruins defenders before roofing the puck upstairs for a sensational goal. The Canadiens would go on to win the Stanley Cup in six games, with Robinson leading the playoffs in assists (17), points (21), and plus-minus (+21), earning him the Conn Smythe Trophy. Widely regarded as one of the greatest defensemen in NHL history, Larry Robinson excelled in every facet of the game —offense, defense, and physical play. With a staggering career plus-minus of +722 — far surpassing any other player in history —Larry Robinson was a two-time Norris Trophy winner and a six-time Stanley Cup champion.

description:
Henrik Lundqvist, celebrated for his outstanding career highlighted by a Vezina Trophy and induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame, showcased his goaltending prowess in the 2012 NHL Winter Classic. Facing off against the Philadelphia Flyers, Lundqvist delivered a crucial moment by making a pivotal save on Daniel Brière's penalty shot with only 19.6 seconds remaining in the third period. This significant stop preserved the team's one-goal lead and helped secure a 3-2 victory.

description:
In the 2023-24 season, Connor Hellebuyck won his second Vezina Trophy as the league’s best goaltender. He posted impressive statistics, including a .921 save percentage, a 2.39 goals-against average, and 37 wins. Additionally, he earned 5 shutouts and helped his team allow the fewest goals against (199) in the league. In a standout sequence, Hellebuyck held strong during a tied third period, stopping multiple chances from Vancouver, which allowed his team to score the game-winner just moments after. In another game against Carolina, he made a crucial save by sliding over just in time to stop Seth Jarvis at the doorstep. Finally, at home against Edmonton, Hellebuyck made two stops on an Evander Kane breakaway. With this achievement, Hellebuyck became the 23rd goaltender in history to win multiple Vezina Trophies.
